# seqout

> Python and R clients for seqout.org, a metadata index over NCBI GEO, NCBI SRA, EBI ENA, DDBJ (DRA and GEA), ArrayExpress and GSA (CNCB-NGDC). Search every archive at once, resolve an accession to its records in the others, and read GEO supplementary files as counts matrices.

The two clients are independent and versioned separately. Both answer from the REST
API at https://seqout.org/api or from DuckDB over remote Parquet files at
https://seqout.org/data, and both default to REST. The backend is always chosen
explicitly, never silently: `connect(backend="parquet")` in Python,
`seqout_connect("parquet")` in R. Parquet answers SQL and works offline, and it is
the only backend for the functions that scan the whole index; REST is current and
needs no extra packages. In R a connection is optional: every function
falls back to a shared REST connection. Every R function is pipe-ready: its subject
is its first argument, with `con` last (`"GSE151530" |> SeqoutGet()`). The calls whose subject
*is* the connection take `con` first instead, so a connection pipes into them
(`SeqoutConnect("parquet") |> RegisterTables()`): `ListJournals`, `ListCenters`,
`ListOrganisms`, `ListAssays`, `ListPlatforms`, `ListLibraryStrategies`,
`ListInstrumentModels`, `SingleCellStudies`, `Tables`, `ClearCache`, `SeqoutClose`,
`SeqoutDefault`, `RegisterTables`, `DownloadDump`. A whole single-cell read is one
chain: `"GSE297547" |> Seqout2Seurat(sample = "GSM8994520")`.

Install:

```bash
# Python library from GitHub (needs Python 3.13+)
uv add "seqout @ git+https://github.com/saketlab/seqout.git#subdirectory=python"
uv add "seqout[counts] @ git+https://github.com/saketlab/seqout.git#subdirectory=python"   # with counts-matrix readers

# using pip
pip install "git+https://github.com/saketlab/seqout.git#subdirectory=python"
pip install "seqout[counts] @ git+https://github.com/saketlab/seqout.git#subdirectory=python"

# CLI tool
uv tool install "seqout @ git+https://github.com/saketlab/seqout.git#subdirectory=python"
```

```r
pak::pak("saketlab/seqout/R")                                              # R package
install.packages("seqout", repos = "https://saketlab.r-universe.dev")      # or r-universe
```

Python:

```python
from seqout import connect, SeqoutListCounts

sq = connect()
sq.seqout_search("liver cancer scRNA", organism="Homo sapiens")
sq.seqout_get("GSE151530").samples

counts = SeqoutListCounts(gse="GSE297547")
counts.manifest()                        # readable units, nothing downloaded yet
counts.matrix(sample="GSM8994520")       # AnnData, cells by genes
counts.design                            # one row per sample
```

R:

```r
library(seqout)

# No connection needed; every function reads the REST API by default
SeqoutGet("GSE151530")
SeqoutGet("GSE151530")$samples
SeqoutSearch("liver cancer scRNA", db = "geo")

counts <- SeqoutListCounts("GSE297547")
SeqoutUnits(counts)
SeqoutMatrix(counts, sample = "GSM8994520")

# Opt in to Parquet for SQL over the whole index
con <- SeqoutConnect("parquet")
Query("SELECT count(*) FROM unified_metadata WHERE n_samples >= 10", con = con)
```

The command line has `seqout search`, `show`, `download`, `pmid`, `author` and
`convert`. `download` takes `--supplementary`, `--sample-supplementary` and
`--fastq` (also `--sra`, `--sra-lite`, `--s3`, `--gcs`). `convert --to` maps an
accession to `study`, `experiment`, `sample`, `run`, `srp`, `srx`, `srs`, `srr`,
`gsm`, `gse`, `pmid` or `doi`, and the `srp-to-pmid` style shorthands do the same.
`seqout parquet download|query|show|set-source` works against the Parquet dump, and
most verbs accept `--parquet [SRC]` to answer with no API request. `--enriched`
returns the ontology labels seqout.org has already prepared; `--norm` produces them
locally with a language model.

In R, alongside search and project metadata, there are `download_*` helpers,
`project_enriched()`, `project_citations(format = "bibtex")`, and `query()` for
raw SQL. `seqout_search()` is the single search entry point. It takes the same
filters as the Python client, given by name. The filters select the full-text or
the structured search. It returns every match, not the first page; give `limit`
to set a maximum. It reads the REST API only. For the Parquet dump, write SQL
with `query()`.

`search_facets()` counts a query's matches per organism, country, assay,
journal, instrument and platform over the whole match set, so a query that
returned too much can be narrowed without paging through it, and
`search_suggest()` corrects a query that returned nothing. The discovery lists
`list_organisms()`, `list_assays()`, `list_platforms()`,
`list_library_strategies()`, `list_instrument_models()`, `list_journals()` and
`list_centers()` enumerate the values a filter will actually match, each with a
count. All of these read the REST API.

In R a connection is not necessary at all: every function has `con` as its last
argument, and the default is a shared REST connection. `query()` needs a Parquet
connection and says so if given a REST one. Its views are DuckDB tables, so
`dplyr` and `dbplyr` work directly on it, and `cache_table()` materialises one
locally.

Search ignores case. `case_sensitive=True` / `case_sensitive = TRUE` (CLI
`--case-sensitive`) keeps only studies whose title or summary has the query
words in the exact case, so `LINE` drops "cell line". It is a full-text filter,
so it cannot be combined with `assay_l1`, `assay_l2` or `geo_*`.

Long-read (PacBio / Oxford Nanopore) studies are a `long_read=True` /
`long_read = TRUE` filter on the ordinary search, restricted to studies with a
long-read experiment in any archive. The collection itself has its own
endpoints: totals (`fetch_longread_summary()` / `LongreadSummary()`), the
filter values (`fetch_longread_facets()` / `LongreadFacets()`), one row per
study (`fetch_longread_projects()` / `LongreadProjects()`, with
`long_read_only`, `chemistries` and `is_single_cell` columns), and one
study's per-run chemistry calls (`fetch_longread_chemistry()` /
`ProjectLongreadChemistry()`). There is no server-side single-cell filter on
the collection, so combining the two filters locally on `is_single_cell`:

```python
# keyword search restricted to long-read studies
sq.search("liver fibrosis", long_read=True)

# the collection itself: long-read-only datasets (no short-read platform
# on the same study)
sq.longread_projects(long_read_only=True, limit=100)

# long-read AND single-cell
sq.longread_projects(single_cell=True, limit=100)
```

```r
# keyword search restricted to long-read studies
SeqoutSearch("liver fibrosis", long_read = TRUE)

# the collection itself: long-read-only datasets
LongreadProjects(long_read_only = TRUE, limit = 100)

# long-read AND single-cell
LongreadProjects(single_cell = TRUE, limit = 100)
```

## Documentation

- [Overview](https://seqout.org/cli/): both clients, install commands and a worked example
- [Python client](https://seqout.org/cli/python/): library, command line and Parquet backend
- [Python installation](https://seqout.org/cli/python/installation/): pip, uv and the optional extras
- [Command line](https://seqout.org/cli/python/cli/): every verb of the `seqout` command, with options
- [Python library](https://seqout.org/cli/python/library/): `connect()`, `Dataset` and the client method surface
- [Parquet backend](https://seqout.org/cli/python/parquet/): querying the Parquet dump with DuckDB, offline or in place
- [Python API reference](https://seqout.org/cli/python/reference/): every public name in the Python package, grouped by task
- [Client reference](https://seqout.org/cli/python/reference/client/): `connect()` and the method surface both backends share
- [Dataset reference](https://seqout.org/cli/python/reference/dataset/): the `Dataset` façade and every field it lazily resolves
- [Search reference](https://seqout.org/cli/python/reference/search/): search, filters and structured queries
- [Counts matrices](https://seqout.org/cli/python/reference/counts/): `SeqoutListCounts` (aka `SeqoutCounts`), manifests, units and readers
- [Utilities reference](https://seqout.org/cli/python/reference/utilities/): retries, resumable downloads and other helpers
- [R package](https://seqout.org/cli/R/): reference index and articles
- [R function reference](https://seqout.org/cli/R/reference/): every exported function, grouped by task
- [Getting started in R](https://seqout.org/cli/R/articles/getting-started.html): the backends, and reading a study
- [Searching in R](https://seqout.org/cli/R/articles/searching.html): the one search function, every filter, and the cost of a large result set
- [Counts and metadata in R](https://seqout.org/cli/R/articles/counts.html): GEO supplementary files to a Seurat object

## Examples

- [Example index](https://seqout.org/cli/python/examples/): every worked example, and what each one covers
- [Command-line examples](https://seqout.org/cli/python/examples/command-line/): the `seqout` command end to end, one shell block per task
- [Getting started](https://seqout.org/cli/python/examples/01_getting_started/): connecting, searching with filters, reading a dataset
- [Working with a dataset](https://seqout.org/cli/python/examples/02_working_with_a_dataset/): every field a `Dataset` holds
- [Accessions and archives](https://seqout.org/cli/python/examples/03_accessions_and_archives/): how an accession from any archive resolves, and when it cannot
- [Offline with Parquet](https://seqout.org/cli/python/examples/04_offline_with_parquet/): the same data with no API request, and where that backend stops
- [Counts and metadata](https://seqout.org/cli/python/examples/05_counts_and_metadata/): a counts matrix with per-cell annotation and study metadata joined in

## Optional

- [Metadata normalization](https://seqout.org/cli/python/normalization/): `--norm`, which labels free-text GEO sample fields with a local language model
- [llms-full.txt](https://seqout.org/cli/llms-full.txt): every page below inlined in one file, including the full API reference
- [Source](https://github.com/saketlab/seqout): both clients, MIT licensed
- [Issues](https://github.com/saketlab/seqout/issues): bug reports and feature requests for either client
- [seqout.org](https://seqout.org): the web interface over the same data
